title: prepr.sh --self-test evals an unterminated step-1a3 block: every run prints a bash syntax error and its null pin passes through it
claim: The self-test's step-1a3 extraction (sed from '# --- 1a3.' to '# --- 1b0.') now ends inside the open `if [ -n "$REUSE" ]; then ... else` that was inserted before 1b0, so the null-control arm's eval raises 1 bash syntax error on every run (the 'eval: syntax error: unexpected end of file' tail of each prepr.sh --self-test), and the pin 'step 1a3 lets a body naming this head run every step' passes on output produced after the parse failure.
mechanism: bash's eval runs complete top-level commands as it parses them, so the leading 1a3 `if` executes (the refuse arm exits 1 inside it, the null arm falls past it), then the parser meets the unterminated REUSE `if` and aborts the eval; `echo FELL-THROUGH` after the eval prints regardless. The null pin keys on FELL-THROUGH alone, never on the eval's status or stderr, so it cannot tell 'the arm let the body through' from 'the eval died'. The block also carries the PREPR_RECORDER_CACHE line, so the self-test writes a stray /tmp/prepr-recpy.<pid>. The pins still pass (rc 0), so the defect is silent: the barrier's drive is no longer the code it says it drives.

evidence.unit: bash syntax errors raised by the self-test's eval of its extracted step-1a3 block (null arm); refuse_pin=1, null_pin=1, block_lines=18
evidence.contention_note: shared compute box; a parse-error count is contention-immune. The same stderr line ends the full prepr.sh --self-test run in sweep.py's N-body-lint-bounce row (rc 0) in a clean git worktree and in the walled export

instrumented_symbol: tools/pr/prepr.sh: the --self-test's blk1a3 extraction and early_head drive (the extraction is read from prepr.sh and run as written)

perturbation.change: the extraction's end anchor moved from '^# --- 1b0\.' to '^# One interpreter resolution' (the first line after step 1a3's fi), in memory (harness --anchor)
perturbation.observed_value: syntax_errors 1 -> 0, block_lines 18 -> 11, refuse_pin and null_pin stay 1

metric_definition: Count of 'syntax error' lines bash writes when the self-test's own blk1a3 extraction is eval'd by its early_head drive with stub arm rc 1 and rc 0.
phenomenon_property: Every block a self-test extracts by line range and evals parses on its own (bash -n clean), and a fall-through pin also asserts the eval returned without a parse error.
seam_rule: python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/s2/prepr_1a3_eval.py   (this seam; the other extracted-and-eval'd blocks of tools/pr/prepr.sh -- bcg, blk1a2, blk3, the take_slot and heavy_skip copies -- were bash -n checked by hand at the baseline and parse)

null_control.note: The pins' verdicts are not what is wrong; the drive under them is.

reproduction_steps: bash tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test (clean git worktree) -> rc 0, output tail 'tools/pr/prepr.sh: eval: line 4017: syntax error: unexpected end of file'
proposed_fix_scope: tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test: end blk1a3's range at step 1a3's own closing fi (or add a '# --- 1a4.' marker before the REUSE block), and make early_head fail on a non-empty eval stderr. A one-line instrument repair (README: made in place, no issue).
